questions.title: Question 1: Binomial Product Expansion, Inequality Modeling & Vector Linear Combinations

parts.prompt:
Expand and simplify completely the algebraic product:
$$(x - y)(3y - 2x)$$
parts.hint: Use the distributive law: multiply each term in the first binomial by every term in the second binomial.

parts.prompt:
Find the truth set of the inequality:
$$3x - 8 \le 4(2 - x)$$
Illustrate your solution on a number line.
parts.hint: Expand the right-hand side first: $3x - 8 \le 8 - 4x$. Collect all terms with x on one side.

parts.prompt:
Given column vectors $$u = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$v = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$$, calculate the vector:
$$\frac{1}{2}\left(u + \frac{1}{2}v\right)$$
parts.hint: Find $\frac{1}{2}v$ first, add to $u$, then multiply the entire vector by $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.title: Question 2: Ladder Incline Trigonometry & Constant Formula Evaluation
questions.diagramSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 230' width='100%' height='210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='30' y1='190' x2='290' y2='190' stroke='#334155' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='240' y1='30' x2='240' y2='190' stroke='#334155' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='60' y1='190' x2='240' y2='50' stroke='#2563eb' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='222' y='172' width='18' height='18' fill='none' stroke='#334155' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='130' y='210' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>Ground = 12 m</text><text x='250' y='125' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#dc2626'>Wall = 16 m</text><text x='125' y='110' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#2563eb'>Ladder L = ?</text><path d='M240,80 A30,30 0 0,1 216,68' fill='none' stroke='#059669' stroke-width='2'/><text x='220' y='95' font-size='11' font-weight='bold' fill='#059669'>θ</text></svg>

parts.prompt:
A ladder leans against a vertical building wall as illustrated above. The top end of the ladder touches the wall at a height of $16\text{ m}$ from the ground, while the foot of the ladder rests $12\text{ m}$ away from the base of the wall.
(i) Calculate the length of the ladder ($L$).
(ii) Find the tangent of the angle ($\theta$) that the ladder makes with the vertical wall in its simplest fractional form.
parts.hint: Apply Pythagoras' theorem: $L^2 = 12^2 + 16^2$. Note that the angle with the wall has opposite side = 12 m and adjacent side = 16 m.
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Ladder length ($L$):**
$$L^2 = 12^2 + 16^2 = 144 + 256 = 400$$
$$L = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ m}$$

**(ii) Tangent with the wall ($\theta$):**
$$\tan \theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = \frac{12\text{ m}}{16\text{ m}} = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$$.

parts.prompt:
Given that $\pi = 3.14$ and $g = 30$, calculate the value of $F$ in the physics relation:
$$F = \frac{3}{4}\pi g^2$$

questions.title: Question 3: Geometric Compass Triangle Construction & Circumcircle Modeling

parts.prompt:
Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only:
(i) Construct triangle $PQR$ such that $|PQ| = 9\text{ cm}$, $\angle QPR = 45^\circ$, and $\angle PQR = 90^\circ$.
(ii) State or calculate the length of side $|QR|$.
parts.hint: Triangle PQR is a right-angled isosceles triangle because angles are 45°, 90°, and 45°.
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Geometric construction:**
- Draw line segment $|PQ| = 9\text{ cm}$.
- Construct a perpendicular ray at $Q$ ($90^\circ$).
- Construct a $45^\circ$ angle at $P$ to meet the perpendicular ray from $Q$ at vertex $R$.

**(ii) Side $|QR|$:**
Since $\angle QPR = 45^\circ$ and $\angle PQR = 90^\circ$, the remaining angle $\angle PRQ = 180^\circ - (90^\circ + 45^\circ) = 45^\circ$.
Since triangle $PQR$ is isosceles, $$|QR| = |PQ| = 9\text{ cm}$$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the length of the hypotenuse $|PR|$ and the total area of triangle $PQR$.

parts.prompt:
Square $ABCD$ has vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(4, 2)$, $C(4, 5)$, and $D(1, 5)$ on the Cartesian plane shown above.
(i) Write down the coordinates of image vertices $A_1, B_1, C_1,$ and $D_1$ under a reflection in the $y$-axis.
(ii) Write down the coordinates of image vertices $A_2, B_2, C_2,$ and $D_2$ under an enlargement from the origin $(0, 0)$ with a scale factor of $k = -1$.
parts.hint: Reflection in y-axis: (x, y) → (-x, y). Enlargement with scale factor -1 from origin: (x, y) → (-x, -y).

parts.prompt: What single geometrical transformation maps square $A_2B_2C_2D_2$ onto square $A_1B_1C_1D_1$?
parts.hint: Compare the coordinates of corresponding points: (-x, -y) maps to (-x, y).
parts.workedSolution:
Notice that for each vertex:
$$A_2(-1, -2) \to A_1(-1, 2)$$
$$B_2(-4, -2) \to B_1(-4, 2)$$
The $x$-coordinate remains unchanged while the $y$-coordinate reverses sign ($y \to -y$).
Therefore, the transformation is a **reflection in the $x$-axis** (or the line $y = 0$).

parts.prompt: Calculate the area of square $ABCD$ in square units.
parts.hint: Side length = difference between consecutive vertices.

questions.title: Question 5: School Canteen Commercial Sales Distribution & Pie Charting
questions.diagramSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 240' width='100%' height='210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='150' cy='120' r='90' fill='#f8fafc' stroke='#334155' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M150,120 L150,30 A90,90 0 0,1 232,84 Z' fill='#bfdbfe' stroke='#1e3a8a'/><path d='M150,120 L232,84 A90,90 0 0,1 217,180 Z' fill='#bbf7d0' stroke='#14532d'/><path d='M150,120 L217,180 A90,90 0 0,1 122,206 Z' fill='#fed7aa' stroke='#7c2d12'/><path d='M150,120 L122,206 A90,90 0 0,1 64,92 Z' fill='#fef08a' stroke='#713f12'/><path d='M150,120 L64,92 A90,90 0 0,1 150,30 Z' fill='#e9d5ff' stroke='#581c87'/><text x='165' y='65' font-size='10' font-weight='bold'>Fanta: 65°</text><text x='195' y='140' font-size='10' font-weight='bold'>Pepsi: 105°</text><text x='140' y='180' font-size='10' font-weight='bold'>Mirinda: 70°</text><text x='75' y='160' font-size='10' font-weight='bold'>Cola: 85°</text><text x='95' y='75' font-size='10' font-weight='bold'>Sprite: 35°</text></svg>

parts.prompt:
The table below shows the distribution of bottles of soft drinks sold by a school canteen in one week:

| Soft Drink | Fanta | Pepsi | Mirinda | Coca-Cola | Sprite |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Bottles Sold | 13 | 21 | 14 | 17 | 7 |

(i) Find the total number of bottles sold.
(ii) Calculate the sector angle for each brand on a pie chart.
parts.modelAnswer: (i) 72 bottles; (ii) Fanta: 65°, Pepsi: 105°, Mirinda: 70°, Coca-Cola: 85°, Sprite: 35°
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Total bottles:**
$$N = 13 + 21 + 14 + 17 + 7 = 72\text{ bottles}$$

**(ii) Sector Angles:**
Each bottle represents $$\frac{360^\circ}{72} = 5^\circ$$.
- **Fanta:** $$13 \times 5^\circ = 65^\circ$$
- **Pepsi:** $$21 \times 5^\circ = 105^\circ$$
- **Mirinda:** $$14 \times 5^\circ = 70^\circ$$
- **Coca-Cola:** $$17 \times 5^\circ = 85^\circ$$
- **Sprite:** $$7 \times 5^\circ = 35^\circ$$
Sum check: $$65^\circ + 105^\circ + 70^\circ + 85^\circ + 35^\circ = 360^\circ$$.

parts.prompt:
(i) What percentage of the total sales was Coca-Cola, correct to one decimal place?
(ii) If a bottle is picked at random from this sales batch, what is the probability that it was Pepsi?
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Percentage of Coca-Cola:**
$$\text{Percentage} = \left(\frac{17}{72}\right) \times 100\% = \frac{1,700}{72}\% \approx 23.61\%$$
Correct to one decimal place: **23.6%**.

**(ii) Probability of Pepsi:**
$$P(\text{Pepsi}) = \frac{21}{72} = \frac{21 \div 3}{72 \div 3} = \frac{7}{24}$$.
